content.text:
I read the disclosure, brief, conversation, request, all seven figure briefs, the numeral ledger, and every draft section, then built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the inventor's own words.

**Ledger highlights (all traced to affirmative USER text in `input/disclosure.md`):**

- **Rail set (10/12/14/16/18):** "elongated straight rail with a flat lower face… A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail. Distance marks are printed along the upper face beside the slot."
- **Fence set (30/32/34/36):** "A fixed fence is attached at the first end… extends downward from the lower face and bears against one straight edge… secured… by two screws received in two corresponding holes… turning the fence over… moves the downwardly projecting part… to the opposite longitudinal side."
- **Spacer plate (40):** "parallel opposite faces and changes the setback of every guided hole by its thickness without changing the separation."
- **Carriage sets (50/52/54/58/60/62 and 70/72/74/78/80/82):** "lower key… prevents the carriage from rotating while allowing it to slide"; "one cylindrical drill bushing with a vertical bore… passes completely through"; "threaded shank… into a clamping shoe below the rail"; each carriage's own pointer "aligned with its bushing axis."
- **Centering set (24/26/94):** "transverse center index at its midpoint"; "shallow V-shaped sight notch… formed in the second end… aligned with the center index"; "align… with a pencil centerline."
- **Claims 1–22:** every limitation, including the negative limitations (claims 11, 22), the material limitations (claims 9, 10, 17), and the method ordering (claim 18) maps to the disclosure's use paragraph and materials paragraph.

**Internal-consistency checks that passed:** every numeral appears in at least one figure brief and means one thing; every parenthetical figure cross-reference in the detailed description points to a figure whose numeral list contains that numeral; section lines 3-3 and 5-5 carry the same designation in FIG. 2, in FIGS. 3/5, and in the Brief Description, with matching carriage assignments; fence-at-left orientation is consistent across FIGS. 1, 2, 6, 7; no drafting notes, placeholders, or unresolved alternatives remain.

**Depiction conventions checked and accepted as confined to the figure briefs:** the plain-block carriages, round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence, schematic slot opening, and graduation-stroke distance marks are each labeled "shown schematically," add no function, and are not verbalized in the application text. Critically, the sight notch is described only as "shallow V-shaped… formed in the second end" — no added depth, taper, angle, runout, or contact topology — and the mounting holes carry no asserted spacing or symmetry. No "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language leaked into `07-drawings.md` or `08-detailed-description.md`.

The review is clean.

Every claim limitation across claims 1-22 (both apparatus independents, the method independent, and all dependents including the negative limitations of claims 11 and 22 and the material limitations of claims 9, 10 and 17), every entry in the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part as it appears in each of the seven figure briefs, every structure, relationship, result, material, position, connection and operating condition in the Summary and Detailed Description, and the Abstract were traced to exact affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md. Representative traces: rail, flat lower face, through-running longitudinal slot and printed distance marks beside the slot to "elongated straight rail with a flat lower face... A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail. Distance marks are printed along the upper face beside the slot"; fence, downwardly projecting portion, two screws and two mounting holes and the reversal to "A fixed fence is attached at the first end... secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding holes. Removing the screws, turning the fence over, and reinstalling the screws moves the downwardly projecting part of the fence from one longitudinal side of the rail to the opposite longitudinal side"; spacer plate to "parallel opposite faces and changes the setback of every guided hole by its thickness without changing the separation between the holes"; keys, cylindrical drill bushings with through bores registering with the slot, parallel bore axes perpendicular to the lower face, clamp knobs with threaded shanks reaching clamping shoes below the rail, and the two independent pointers to the corresponding carriage and clamping paragraphs; transverse center index at the midpoint, shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with it, and the pencil centerline to "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint. A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index"; hardened-metal replaceable bushings and rigid polymer or metal for the remaining parts to the closing materials paragraph; and the no-motor, no-battery, no-sensor, no-network limitations to "The tool has no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection." The method steps and their order match the disclosure's "To use the tool" paragraph, including tightening before placement and the lift-away step with no part remaining attached. Internal-consistency checks all passed: each numeral has exactly one meaning and appears in at least one figure brief; every parenthetical figure cross-reference in the description points to a figure whose numeral list contains that numeral (58 in FIGS. 1 and 5, 78 in FIGS. 1 and 3, 14 in FIG. 4, 12 in FIGS. 3 and 5, 40 in FIG. 4, 26 and 94 in FIG. 7, 34 and 36 in FIG. 6); the section-line designations 3-3 and 5-5 repeat identically in the source view FIG. 2, in the resulting views FIGS. 3 and 5, and in the Brief Description, with FIG. 3 consistently through the second guide carriage 70 and FIG. 5 through the first guide carriage 50; the fence-at-left orientation is consistent across FIGS. 1, 2, 6 and 7; claims and description use the same relationships and preserve every term required by the brief (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch); no means-plus-function language appears; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. Drawing conventions were audited against the functional-surface rule: the plain-block carriages, round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence, schematic elongated slot opening and graduation-stroke distance marks are each expressly labeled "shown schematically," add no technical function or relationship, and are not verbalized in the application text; the sight notch is stated only as "shallow V-shaped... formed in the second end," with no added depth, taper, angle, runout direction or contact topology, and the mounting holes carry no asserted spacing, symmetry or count beyond the disclosed two. The offset cutting planes are drafting conventions whose stepped legs follow necessarily from the disclosed fact that the bore and the knob shank both pass through the same slot. No "by way of example," "any closed outline," or other embodiment-broadening language justifying a renderer choice appears in draft/07-drawings.md or draft/08-detailed-description.md. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later citation review as instructed. No unsupported technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found.
